newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The Capital Market Commission yesterday imposed fines ranging from 1.6 million drachmas to 15.9 million on main shareholders of 24 listed companies for violating disclosure regulations on changes of ownership stakes.The highest fine was imposed on Socrates Kokkalis, of Intracom.
--Tension between pharmaceutical companies and the health ministry continues as firms demand changes to the manner of payment of debts owed them by state-run hospitals.

--Ergobank is showing interest in a number of planned sales of state-run banks, such as Ionian, Macedonia-Thrace and General. The Ionian bank - when it is put on the market - is expected to draw much buyer interest, given its existing network and levels of staff.

--The national economy ministry is examining a clause in a recently concluded wage agreement at Olympic Airways which will give employees a 40 percent rise over basic wages. A meeting at the ministry yesterday with the directors of public transport organisations revealed that the wage bill for public utilities in 1996 at times exceeded 80 percent.
IMERISIA

--The government and Bank of Greece have decided that they will not place limitations on the level of fluctuation of the drachma and that it will rely on market conditions, a new element to exchange and interest policies currently being followed.

--The sale of state-run enterprises is expected to inject 250 billion drachmas into state coffers this year. The government has given priority to a second float of 12 percent of OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation.
--The Agricultural Bank of Greece will proceed with a wider programme of exploiting its assets, beginning with the establishment of two subsidiaries.
KERDOS
--The government will float 12.0 percent of OTE by the end of May and hopes to cull 240 billion drachmas from the offer. The shares will be priced 5.0 percent lower than current market prices.
--The finance ministry is seeking ways to avert misuse of cheaper heating fuel. Heating fuel has been found in use in vehicles, farm machinery and industry.
EXPRESS
--The state-run gas distribution company will follow OTE to the stock exchange and will be followed by duty-free stores.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou has decided to abolish the Organisation for Ailing Enterprises - which handles all state companies running into trouble - within two years, signalling a speeding up of procedures to sell off problematic firms.

--A new tender for Cretabank is being considered, following lone bidder Bank of Piraeus's withdrawal of their offer. The publication of Cretabank's 1996 fiscal results - expected to be slightly better than the previous year - is expected to spur interest.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The first reactions from the investing public to the reduction of returns from state titles were seen by the 100 billion drachma shortfall in zero coupons.

--Tomorrow's 24-hour general strike will top off a week of labour unrest. The government remains unmoved in the face of continuing strikes by seamen and teachers and impending protests by farmers, while judicial officials are prepared to prosecute those obstructing public transport. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
